requirement.evidence: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
requirement.note: Document D081 states the prohibition on sale/use and the civil action right; occupancy management is also stated.

key_value.evidence: Each month of use for each affected dwelling unit may constitute a separate violation, and tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C(b) and (d).
key_value.note: D002 supports the $1,000 per violation and per unit per month exposure.

effective_date.evidence: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024.

status.evidence: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
status.note: Presented as current law; D002 (Aug 2026) shows it is being enforced in litigation.

coverage.note: Coverage is null on the card.

citation.evidence: alleging that Greystar violated San Francisco Administrative Code § 37.10C through its alleged use of RealPage and Yardi products.
citation.note: D081 refers to Section 37.10C of the Rent Ordinance; D002 gives S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.
